ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

 

The con

responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug

The U.S. Government intends to award a contract to the responsible offeror representing best value using comparative evaluation authorized under FAR 13.106-2(b) (3). A comparative evaluation is defined as the act of comparing two or more offers in response to the RFQ. The item-by-item comparison is performed by comparing each offer directly to one another to determine which provides the best value to the Department. Comparative evaluation is NOT a low price technically acceptable (LPTA) or trade-off process. Prospective offers must still meet basic standards for responsibility at FAR 9.104 and solicitation compliance to be eligible for award. We intend to award a contract based on initial quotations, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies if there is a need to do so. The Procurement Office will not be holding a pre-quotation conference for this RFQ. However, we will accept questions regarding these requirements until November 16, 2026, via email: PristinaProcurement@state.gov . To meet these ESR bunch injection schemes and requirements, an array of stripline-based kickers, individually fed by high voltage (HV) pulse signals of up to +/-30 kV, will be installed in the ESR. The required deflection angle is in the range 1- 1.5 mrad, for the individual stripline kicker we target a deflection angle of ~125 µrad @ 18 GeV, assuming +/-27 kV pulse supply voltage between the kicker electrodes. To keep the losses of the stored beam low, a ~15 σ distance between the stored beam and the injection septa in the ESR must be maintained, which translates into a minimum physical aperture of 30 mm diameter for the stripline kickers.
